key_insight: Radiomic shape and frozen foundation-model distance scores can flag segmentation failures post hoc, while within-site evaluation reveals errors that pooled rankings may obscure.
clinical_relevance: These scores could support quality-control review of prostate and hippocampus MRI segmentations when deployed models are black boxes.
method: Measure Mahalanobis distance from predicted-mask radiomic shape features to a labeled reference set.
Overlay masks on images, encode with frozen DINOv3, and use mask-weighted patch pooling to compute a second distance score.
Rank cases by failure risk without registration or access to segmentation-model internals.
evidence_signal: On multi-site prostate and hippocampus MRI under protocol and population shifts, both scores were competitive with Atlas-RCA and ensemble pairwise-Dice baselines for within-site ranking.
watch_item: Report both pooled and within-site performance: strong pooled rankings can reflect site difficulty rather than reliable detection of individual failures.
paper_title: Foundation Model and Radiomics Distance Scores for Post-Hoc Segmentation Failure Detection
